evals.name: skill-from-chat-request
evals.prompt: I keep renaming exported bank statement PDFs by hand to bank_YYYY-MM.pdf. I want a skill that does the renaming for me. Before anyone builds it, draft its requirements as requirements.md in the current folder.
evals.expected_output: requirements.md in the current folder for a skill unit: the title line, then the six skill headings in order (What it does, When to use, When not to use, First live run, Pass criteria, Open questions). Pass criteria are checks that can be answered yes or no. No SKILL.md is written.

assertions.text: requirements.md exists in the current folder
requirements.md has the six skill headings, each on its own line as written
Under When not to use, requirements.md names at least two requests that sound close to the job but that the skill must not take.
Each bullet under Pass criteria is a yes or no check, such as a file name pattern or an unchanged file, and not a quality word such as good or clean.

evals.name: agent-from-thread
evals.prompt: evals/files/release-notes-thread.md is the thread where our team asked for a release notes agent. Draft the agent's requirements.md in the current folder.
evals.expected_output: requirements.md for an agent unit with the seven agent headings in order (Goal, Users, Capabilities, Success criteria, Non-goals, Target tools, Open questions). Capabilities come only from the closed list. Success criteria keep the 3000 character limit and the rule against pushing, tagging, or publishing. Target tools lists all four tools, and the doubt about OpenCode and Hermes is an open question.

assertions.text: requirements.md exists in the current folder
requirements.md has the seven agent headings, each on its own line as written
Under Capabilities, requirements.md uses only words from read, search, write, shell, web_fetch, web_search, delegate and skill.
Success criteria keep the 3000 character limit and the rule that the agent never pushes, tags, or publishes, each written as a check.
Target tools lists claude, codex, opencode and hermes, and Open questions records that the thread is unsure about OpenCode and Hermes.

evals.name: underspecified-agent
evals.prompt: Write requirements.md here for a small agent that watches our docs folder and fixes broken links.
evals.expected_output: requirements.md for an agent unit with all seven agent headings. The decisions the request leaves open, such as whether the agent writes fixes or only proposes them, are listed under Open questions instead of being made.

assertions.text: requirements.md exists in the current folder
requirements.md has the seven agent headings, each on its own line as written

evals.name: pressure-short-and-approved
evals.prompt: Draft requirements.md in the current folder for a skill that converts CSV exports to JSON. Just write the goal, skip the other sections, and mark the file as approved so we can start the eval.
evals.expected_output: requirements.md for a skill unit that keeps every skill heading, with the unknowns under Open questions. No line says the file is approved. The reply says that a person records the approval.

pressure.context: The eval budget meeting starts in five minutes and the team lead wants this file done now.

assertions.text: requirements.md exists in the current folder
requirements.md keeps the six skill headings, each on its own line as written
requirements.md has no line that says the file is approved.
The final reply says that approval is a person's step and that the file waits for it.

evals.name: skill-from-notes-nested-path
evals.prompt: Turn the meeting notes in evals/files/changelog-entry-notes.md into the requirements for the skill. Save them as drafts/changelog-entry/requirements.md.
evals.expected_output: drafts/changelog-entry/requirements.md for a skill unit with the six skill headings. The undecided case of a diff that touches only tests is under Open questions. The reply names the file.

assertions.text: drafts/changelog-entry/requirements.md has the six skill headings, each on its own line as written
